text:
sophie: Heads up - I'm drafting a short PR for a 'self-hosted blueprint' rollout. Want to lock minimal launch criteria and the installer profiles. Punting coordination to this thread instead of a giant doc.
ravi: Good call. Can we be concrete about must-haves? Field keeps asking about who owns egress IPs and what happens to routing during upgrades.
sophie: Current sketch of must-haves:
1) Opinionated installer profiles (minimal / core / full)
2) Customer-network stewarding doc + sample BGP snippet
3) Zero-downtime agent upgrade plan (drain/warm/cache)
4) KMS + cert rotation path (HSM optional)
5) Airgap-friendly bundle and offline installer.
Missing anything obvious?
mike: Add a migration-mode flag so ops can opt into staged rolling upgrades. Example CLI:
``nredwood-install --profile core --mode migration --migration-window '02:00-05:00'
```
Also expose `--operator-overlay` for canary runs.
ana: Zero-downtime plan should be operator-overlay + sidecar drain hook. Tested flow: drain -> warm kvcache -> flip traffic. Need a TL;DR for field-runbooks.
jen: Field asks we can't ignore: allowed egress IP ranges for customer firewall whitelists, and a fallback 'relay' plan when outbound is blocked. Can we ship a tiny relay binary instead of a full proxy?
sophie: Egress ranges = yes. Relay binary is doable but increases ops surface. Proposal: light-weight 'edge-proxy' (single static binary) + health endpoints. If customer refuses outbound we fallback to relay-mode with explicit consent.
ravi: Edge-proxy works. Also we need an explicit trust-boundary diagram: which certs are customer-owned vs control-plane managed. That should be in the steward doc.
mike: I'll draft the network diagram. Also suggest supporting both customer-provided certs (via KMS/HSM) and managed certs. Docs must call out feature gates that require customer certs.
ana: On upgrades - hosted auto-updates don't apply for private. For private: pin-by-default, with a canary rollout pattern. SLO goal: <1% failed requests during an upgrade window for canaryed customers. Sound reasonable?
sophie: +1. Add to launch criteria: published runbook + automated upgrade test-suite + canary operator pattern.
deploy-bot: buildbot: artifact redwood-selfhost:v2026.03.15-rc1 created. link: https://artifacts/redwood/sha256/abc123
jen: Sweet. After rc1 let's run the ACME corp canary (they volunteered). Field team can do shadow monitoring.
ravi: Prefer Wed 02:00 UTC next week for the canary. Field team ready to shadow.
mike: I'll add a `--dry-run` flag to the installer so customers can simulate network checks. Example:
``nredwood-install --profile core --dry-run --check-egress 8.8.8.8:443
```
Dry-run will print suggested firewall rules and show which ports we attempt to reach.
ana: One more: telemetry for private installs must be minimal and opt-in. If collected, use hashed IDs and clear consent. Add as mandatory security checklist item.
sophie: Agreed. Next steps: mike -> installer flags PR; jen -> coordinate ACME canary; ana -> upgrade runbook and drain diagram; ravi -> network steward doc with BGP sample; i'll assemble the launch checklist and post back by Friday. Thanks everyone :thumbsup: 
sophie: (closing note) If anyone hits blockers, drop short notes here; we'll triage in the sync on Thursday.
